steps.sql: SET lock_timeout = '3s'; ALTER TABLE orders ADD COLUMN customer_id_new bigint;

steps.note: trigger keeps it in sync for new and updated rows
steps.sql: CREATE FUNCTION orders_sync_customer() RETURNS trigger LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$ BEGIN NEW.customer_id_new := NEW.customer_id; RETURN NEW; END $$;SET lock_timeout = '3s'; CREATE TRIGGER orders_sync_customer BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE ON orders FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION orders_sync_customer();

DO $$ DECLARE lo bigint := 0; hi bigint; BEGIN SELECT max(id) INTO hi FROM orders; WHILE lo <= hi LOOP UPDATE orders SET customer_id_new = customer_id WHERE id > lo AND id <= lo + 50000 AND customer_id_new IS NULL; COMMIT; lo := lo + 50000; END LOOP; END $$;

steps.note: customer_id_new: NOT NULL via a validated CHECK
steps.sql: SET lock_timeout = '3s'; ALTER TABLE orders ADD CONSTRAINT customer_id_new_not_null CHECK (customer_id_new IS NOT NULL) NOT VALID;

steps.note: validate the check (scans, but doesn't block writes)
steps.sql: ALTER TABLE orders VALIDATE CONSTRAINT customer_id_new_not_null;

steps.note: SET NOT NULL (instant: the check proves it), drop the check
steps.sql: SET lock_timeout = '3s'; ALTER TABLE orders ALTER COLUMN customer_id_new SET NOT NULL; ALTER TABLE orders DROP CONSTRAINT customer_id_new_not_null;

steps.note: swap the columns in one short transaction
steps.sql: SET lock_timeout = '3s'; BEGIN; ALTER TABLE orders DROP COLUMN customer_id; ALTER TABLE orders RENAME COLUMN customer_id_new TO customer_id; DROP TRIGGER orders_sync_customer ON orders; COMMIT; DROP FUNCTION orders_sync_customer();
